I identify NaEu(MoO4)2 (mp-1221078) as the only phase present. I matched the peaks by eye and did not calculate a fit score.

- **NaEu(MoO4)2 matches.** I simulated this candidate. Its strongest peak, near 28.8°, lines up with the dominant observed peak. Its weaker peaks also line up: about 15.3°, the pair at 18.3–18.6°, the peaks near 31–34°, and the strong pair near 49° (observed at about 23 each, simulated at about 17 and 16). The later observed peaks near 57–60° also fit its simulated peaks there.
- **Li4TiV3O8 does not match.** I simulated this candidate too. It puts its strongest peak near 18.5° and a second strong pair in the 30s. The observed pattern has nothing close to those strengths.
- **The rest were not simulated.** I found no clear leftover peak above the noise that would need a second phase. Because I didn't simulate the other seven candidates, a weak minor phase can't be fully ruled out.
